ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AD=DC$. If $\angle BAD=20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle C$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given:
\[ \because AB=AD \]
\[ \therefore \angle ABD=\angle ADB=\frac{180^\circ-\angle BAD}{2}=\frac{180^\circ-20^\circ}{2}=80^\circ \]
\[ \because DA=DC \]
\[ \therefore \angle C=\angle DAC \]
Since $\angle ADB$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ADC$,
\[ \therefore \angle ADB=\angle C+\angle DAC \]
\[ \therefore 80^\circ=\angle C+\angle C \]
Solving, we find $\angle C=\boxed{40^\circ}$
